Visual Studio Code

Keep development, debugging, and source review together.

VSOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Visual Studio Code is an editor with language support, source control, debugging, and extensions. We can set up a reproducible workspace for a website or application so engineers can inspect the code, run the project, and diagnose issues consistently. Its role in a client engagement is the development environment; the delivered product remains independently deployable software.

Useful outputs

  • Documented workspace setup
  • Repeatable run, debug, and review tasks
  • Developer onboarding and troubleshooting notes

Where we can apply it

  • Engineer onboarding: repository → local setup → verified run task.
  • API diagnosis: request reproduction → debugger inspection → reviewed source fix.
  • Release preparation: change review → local checks → CI handoff.
01

Use case 1

Create a shared project workspace with documented run and debug commands.

02

Use case 2

Inspect integration failures using breakpoints and meaningful application logs.

03

Use case 3

Review source changes alongside the project's Git history and delivery tasks.

Inputs we need

  • Project repository and supported runtime versions
  • Developer setup requirements and extensions
  • Debug configuration and local environment samples

Delivery sequence

  • Configure the repository's runtime, formatting, and workspace conventions.
  • Add run and debug tasks suited to the actual application.
  • Verify a new developer can start the project from the documentation.

Expert review points

  • Review extension access and workspace trust requirements.
  • Keep real secrets outside tracked workspace configuration.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.
